mathdb_title: Integer-coefficient conjecture for Wronskian Hermite polynomials

literal_scope.statement: For every partition lambda, He_lambda(x) in Z[x], where He_lambda := Wr[He_{n_1},...,He_{n_r}] / Delta(n_lambda), n_i = lambda_i + r - i (probabilists' He_n, monic), Delta(n_lambda) = prod_{i<j} (n_j - n_i).
literal_scope.normalization: monic after division by the Vandermonde of the degree sequence
literal_scope.source_conjecture: arXiv:1801.07980v1 Conjecture 3.7; source rationality remark and Maple check |lambda| <= 35

source_evidence.paper: N. Bonneux, M. Stevens, Recurrence Relations for Wronskian Hermite Polynomials, arXiv:1801.07980 (2018); SIGMA 14 (2018) 048

successor_evidence.paper: N. Bonneux, Z. Hamaker, J. Stembridge, M. Stevens, Wronskian Appell Polynomials and Symmetric Functions, arXiv:1812.01864v2; published Advances in Applied Mathematics, DOI 10.1016/j.aam.2019.101932 (2019)
resolving_results: Theorem 5.8: Appell sequence with cumulants c_k (eq. (3.9)) satisfying c_k/(k-1)! in Z for all k >= 1 implies A_lambda in Z[x] for all partitions lambda.
Corollary 7.1: For any partition lambda, He_lambda in Z[x] — explicitly confirming arXiv:1801.07980 Conjecture 3.7.
successor_evidence.applicability_chain: Probabilists' Hermite is Appell with exp(xt - t^2/2): c_1 = 0, c_2 = -1, c_k = 0 for k >= 3; hence c_k/(k-1)! in Z. Definition (1.2) of A_lambda is byte-for-byte the same monic normalization as source Definition 2.2 (successor cites [6, Lemma 2.1]).
successor_evidence.proof_mechanism: Ring homomorphism phi_A from symmetric functions: phi_A(H(lambda) s_lambda) = A_lambda (Theorem 4.1); H(lambda) s_lambda in Z[p_mu] (Macdonald I.7 Ex. 17(a)); phi_A(p_n) = c_n/(n-1)! (Proposition 4.3).
